title: Save Time with These Meal-Prepping Tips
paragraphs: Do you often feel too busy to cook healthy meals during the week? Meal prepping, which means preparing meals or ingredients in advance, can help you save time. Here are some tips to help you do it safely and effectively.
Choose one day, such as Sunday, to cook several meals at once. Then, divide the food into containers for the days ahead. This means you only need to heat up a meal when you are busy.
Do not prepare too far ahead

Cooked food does not last forever. According to the US Department of Agriculture (USDA), cooked meals and leftovers should only be kept in the refrigerator for three to four days. Because of this, food safety experts say that you should not prepare a whole week of meals and keep them all in the fridge.

If you want to prepare meals for the whole week, you can freeze some of them. According to the USDA, cooked meals can be kept in the freezer for three to four months. However, not every food freezes well, so it is a good idea to choose recipes that are suitable for freezing.
Put cooked food in the refrigerator within two hours of making it. Dividing food into shallow containers will help it cool down faster.
Write the date on each container. This way, you will always know how long the food has been in the fridge.
Finally, if food changes color, smells bad or tastes strange, do not eat it. When in doubt, throw it out.
